content.user_title: Apply Test-Driven Development to Every Change
content.value_statement: Software changes often grow before their expected behavior is verified. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused Red-Green-Refactor cycles.
actual_capabilities: Structures feature work into Red, Green, and Refactor phases.
Requires a correctly failing test before production implementation.
Guides minimal implementation until each selected test passes.
Encourages behavior-focused test names and assertions.
Provides checklists for tests, implementation, and refactoring.
limitations: Does not select or configure a testing framework.
Does not replace integration, performance, or security testing.
Requires an existing project where tests can be executed.
Does not define domain requirements or acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Build a Small Feature
use_cases.description: Turn one behavior into a failing test, minimal implementation, and focused refactoring.

use_cases.title: Fix a Reproducible Defect
use_cases.description: Capture a defect with a failing regression test before changing production behavior.

use_cases.title: Teach Incremental Design
use_cases.description: Demonstrate how successive tests drive a general solution from a simple starting point.

prompt_templates.title: Start One TDD Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Use TDD to add [behavior]. First write one focused test, explain the expected failure, then implement only enough to pass.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner is adding one clear behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Bug with TDD
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce [bug] with one failing regression test. Confirm why it fails, apply the smallest fix, then suggest a focused refactor.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer has a repeatable defect.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Incremental Test Cases
prompt_templates.prompt: List the behaviors for [feature] from simplest to most complex. Begin the first Red-Green-Refactor cycle and stop after one passing test.
prompt_templates.scenario: A feature needs an ordered TDD path.

prompt_templates.title: Drive a Complex Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [module] and its tests. Identify observable behavior, add characterization tests incrementally, and refactor only while all tests remain green.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced developer is changing established code.

output_examples.input: Add support for an empty shopping cart total.
output: Red: Add one test expecting an empty cart total of zero.
Green: Return zero for the empty-cart case.
Refactor: Remove duplication only after the test passes.

output_examples.output: First add a regression test proving that an existing email is rejected. Then make the smallest validation change and rerun all tests.

output_examples.input: Plan TDD for a username formatter.
output: Start with lowercasing one simple username.
Add whitespace handling only after the first test passes.
Add punctuation and empty-input cases in later cycles.

best_practices: Confirm each new test fails for the expected reason.
Change one behavior at a time and keep feedback cycles short.
Refactor only with a passing test suite.
anti_patterns: Do not write production behavior before observing a failing test.
Do not add many tests before making the first test pass.
Do not assert private implementation details when public behavior is available.

faq.question: What workflow does this skill follow?
faq.answer: It follows Red-Green-Refactor: write a failing test, make it pass minimally, then improve the design.

faq.question: Can it choose my testing framework?
faq.answer: No. It works with project context but does not prescribe or configure a framework.

faq.question: Does every test need one assertion?
faq.answer: The skill recommends one focused assertion so each failure communicates one behavior clearly.

faq.question: Can I use it for bug fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. Start with a failing regression test that reproduces the defect before changing production code.

faq.question: When should refactoring begin?
faq.answer: Begin refactoring only after the selected test and the full relevant suite pass.

faq.question: Does this replace other testing methods?
faq.answer: No. Continue using integration, system, performance, accessibility, and security tests when the project requires them.
